boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Donaldsonville record (August 9, 1862) in Operations Against Baton Rouge [July-August 1862]. The live campaign label reads Confederate Offensive Against Baton Rouge. The firing on the Sallie Robinson, the Brooklyn and the St. Charles before August 9 is context. The destruction of the Arkansas on August 6, the evacuation of Baton Rouge on August 20 and the occupation of Port Hudson are context; multi-action totals are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Three Navy ships [US] and a few partisans [CS]; the live field reads zero. The St. James committee says two sloops of war and one gunboat under Farragut anchored before the town and landed a force; Farragut names no count. No inspected passage gives the number of partisans.
claims.rationale: Unit identifications and a ship count from an interested civilian report. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Farragut says he heard firing from the town on the Sallie Robinson and the Brooklyn and that the St. Charles was fired on the next night; his August 8 order says Renshaw had told him the town was warned after the Empire Parish was fired into. The committee says no armed vessels had been assailed.
claims.rationale: Attributed knowledge from interested documents on each side; the committee's statement and Farragut's account of the Brooklyn differ.

claims.value: Farragut ordered notice given to send women and children out of Plaquemine and Donaldsonville because he intended to destroy them for firing into his vessels, and a printed proclamation over his name says a portion of the town would be burned each time his boats were fired on. The committee resolved to ask Governor Moore to avert further destruction.
claims.rationale: Stated aims from interested documents on each side.

claims.value: Farragut ordered the destruction and signed as Flag-Officer; he names Phillippe Landry as said to be a captain of guerrillas who fired on his men and was chased off. The frozen commanders are Captain Phillippe Landry and Rear Admiral David G. Farragut; the live page gives Farragut as Admiral.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested documents; Landry's command is reported only as hearsay. The listed commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and neither the frozen nor the live naval rank is adopted.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory (inconclusive); the live result reads Union Victory. Farragut says he fulfilled his promise to a certain extent, burning the hotels, wharf buildings and Landry's houses; the committee says the most valuable portion of the town and an adjacent plantation's buildings were consumed. NPS says firing on Union ships generally ceased afterwards.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The frozen and live results differ in qualification; the later cessation of firing is not tested by the inspected documents.

open_questions: Bell's August 9 report (read, not selected), the ships' logs of the Hartford, Brooklyn and Cayuga for August 9, any Confederate or parish record of the partisans, and a history covering the action remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Farragut's August 8 order, August 10 report and printed proclamation, and the St. James Parish committee's August 11 report, are separate families printed in the Official Records of the Navies, Series I, Volume 19, a shared container. No history covering this action was found in the inspected passages of Irwin or Mahan, so this record has two families beyond NPS; the gap is recorded. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
